answer: A cipher keeps each ballot quiet until its own tide: sealed vote, key freed on a clock no farm sets twice. The reveal ripples through ten random peers, each stamping arrival time. Lockstep farms die by the ripple check: ten ballots in one 40 ms window burn together, stakes slashed. Each ballot carries a $25 ember smoldering six tides, returned only if its ripple stays irregular. LayerZero flagged 803,093 addresses on timing like this. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 keys, 7,500 agent-hours, $250,000 frozen. One ember cools slow; ten lit at once is one hand striking matches.
